questions.q: Tell me about a Java application you worked on. What did it do, which frameworks did you use, and which part did you build yourself?
questions.looks_for: Clear description of the system, real frameworks (for example Spring Boot, Hibernate), their own modules or features, and the outcome. Honest about team versus individual work.

questions.q: Describe a production issue in a Java service that you helped solve. How did you find the cause?
questions.looks_for: Uses logs, stack traces, monitoring, thread or heap dumps as relevant. Explains the actual cause, the fix, and what was done to stop it happening again.

questions.q: Your Java service's memory keeps growing until it crashes every few days. How would you investigate?
questions.looks_for: Suspects a memory leak, takes and compares heap dumps, looks for growing collections, caches without limits, unclosed resources or listeners, and checks garbage collection logs. Tests the fix.

questions.q: When would you use an interface versus an abstract class in Java, and why does it matter for maintaining code?
questions.looks_for: Explains interfaces as contracts that many unrelated classes can implement, abstract classes for shared code and state, and connects it to flexibility, testing and loose coupling.

questions.q: Two threads update the same account balance at the same time and the final value is wrong. Why does this happen and how would you fix it?
questions.looks_for: Identifies a race condition from non-atomic read-modify-write. Fixes with synchronization, locks, atomic classes, or database-level locking or transactions, and mentions trade-offs like contention.

questions.q: Just before a release, you find that a feature you built passes tests but gives wrong results for one rare type of customer. What do you do?
questions.looks_for: Raises it immediately with the lead, explains the impact honestly, suggests options (fix now, feature flag, delay, or release with known issue), and adds a test for the case.

questions.q: Why do you want to work as a Java developer, and what do you want to grow into? Please state clearly your notice period or joining date, and your expected salary in ₹ per month or per year?
questions.looks_for: Gives a genuine reason tied to the work, a sensible growth direction, a clear notice period or joining date, and a clear salary figure or range in ₹. Honest about buyout or negotiable notice if relevant.
